content.overview:
Welcome to auto-mcs! This software provides a simple and easy-to-digest experience for those who want to play Minecraft with their friends without the hassle of server installation & maintenance.

## some notable features include:
- create a server in less than a minute
- full support for Paper, Fabric, Forge, CraftBukkit, Spigot, and Vanilla
- automatic server installation & updates
- ability to import any existing server
- switch worlds, versions, and distributions on the fly
- automatic back-up management
- custom console with a scripting API
- detailed crash detection with an easily viewable report
- internal mod & plugin browser/installer (auto-mcs can update plugins as well)
- firewall-like Access Control menu to manage bans, whitelist, and operators from a single page
- built-in server.properties editor for ease of use and key protection
- and much more...
content.installation:
To get started, download the [latest version of auto-mcs](<https://auto-mcs.com/download>). Extract auto-mcs from the `.zip` file to a location of your choice and launch it. That's it, there's no installation required!

> *Note:*  **If you're using Linux, you might need to run `chmod +x auto-mcs` to give the binary executable permission**

To start using auto-mcs, you can create a new server from scratch or import a server you've made on your own. As with any Minecraft server, auto-mcs requires Java and it will be installed and managed internally. It might take a minute to initialize on your first server operation.

> *Note:*  **For advanced users wanting to leverage remote access, Docker, or headless functionality, please view the [Telepath guide](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/telepath>)**
content.create a server:
For the majority of users, auto-mcs is pre-configured to provide optimal settings. Choose an instant template to get started! Using a template automatically enables the playit integration to make it easy for your friends to join.

> *Note:*  **If you want people to join over the internet, you will need to [port forward or setup the built-in proxy](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started#wan/internet-configuration>)**
content.modpack setup: To install a modpack, click the “Modpack” button in the create server menu. You can either download one directly from Modrinth, or import your own `.zip` file. If you’re downloading it yourself, be sure to download the server pack specifically.
content.advanced setup:
You can modify just about anything during the setup process. Below is documentation to assist with all available configurations. - server type This menu provides the ability to augment the base feature set of your server. There are a variety of distributions to choose from, some of which include additional capabilities such as modding APIs and performance tweaks. If you want to install mods/plugins with a supported distribution, auto-mcs provides an add-on manager to import or download plugins directly. This can be accessed through the additional options by clicking ‘[Add-on Manager’](). After your server is created, the distribution can be switched at any time with the ‘Change server.jar’ button in the [server settings.]()Note: the amscript plugin API is an auto-mcs feature available with any distributionvanillaVanilla Minecraft is the stock experience that provides no additional capabilities apart from the core game-play features. Vanilla is recommended for most users since it has optimal support for the game mechanics such as Redstone, command blocks, and datapacks. This comes at the cost of performance in some instances. Another advantage of vanilla is that it’s the most up to date as everything else is based on it. When there’s a new update it can take a week or so for other distributions to update as well.paperA high-performance, extensible, lightweight server based on Spigot. Paper provides numerous advantages over vanilla such as asynchronous chunk loading, rendering enhancements, and Redstone optimization which can be extremely useful with lower-end hardware. Like other CraftBukkit/Spigot-based servers, some of these optimizations can cause issues with stock mechanics like Redstone. In addition to these features, Paper has a suite of cutom plugins and supports all Spigot and CraftBukkit plugins as well. [Learn more about Paper]()spigotSpigot aims to provide an experience as close to vanilla as possible, with the addition of plugin support. It also implements many of the same performance improvements like asynchronous chunk loading. With this in mind, it can be more hardware intensive than Paper depending on the configuration. [Learn more about Spigot]()craftbukkitThe original server-side plugin API for extending the capabilities of multiplayer Minecraft. (CraftBukkit/Bukkit) has since been forked and superseded by modern solutions such as Paper. It has been provided in auto-mcs for compatibility with legacy servers. [Learn more about CraftBukkit]()fabricFabric is a modern server and client-side modding API for injecting custom assets into the game. This allows for new features and redesigns of the core gameplay. The Fabric API is automatically included with the installation of Fabric through auto-mcs. Mods need to be installed on both the server and any client that connects. [Learn more about Fabric]()forgeForge is a modding platform with years of support and a large library of additional content. Similar to Fabric, it has server and client-side functionality with the requirement of having mods on both the server and any client that connects. [Learn more about Forge]() - server version The version of Minecraft you choose is responsible for the core mechanics and features with game-play. It’s recommended to use the latest version (configured by default) for security purposes unless there’s a reason not to:Trying unreleased betas (snapshots)Utilizing legacy Redstone/command block projectsMods that require an older versionBarring this recommendation, auto-mcs supports and can manage every version of Minecraft that’s available. [Learn more about the different versions here]()Generally, all clients that connect are required to use the same game version that your server is running. > *Note:* **If your server runs Paper, Spigot or Fabric, it’s possible to use ViaVersion to enable cross-version capabilities. [Learn more here]()** - Trying unreleased betas (snapshots) - Utilizing legacy Redstone/command block projects - Mods that require an older version - world select The level/world is a folder that contains the block and player data of your server. There are a couple options for selecting a world:create a new world(default) this option will generate a server from scratch when the server is started. A custom seed and level type can be specified.import a worldTo import a world that you’ve previously made or have downloaded, click on the ‘create new world’ label or `BROWSE`Type in a world name or browse to the root folder of your save. The world will be checked for compatibility and if successful, it will replace the text in the import world input. After your server is created, the world file can be re-generated or replaced at any time by clicking on ‘Change World File’ in the [server settings](). - networking Your server’s network configuration is one of the most important aspects in terms of accessibility and security. Generally, it’s unnecessary to configure the Local Area Network (LAN) aspect of the server. The Wide Area Network (WAN) configuration is imperative if you wish for clients to connect publicly over the internet.
# LAN configurationThe IP/port combo box can be configured with an IP, a port, or both. Generally, you’d want to modify the port if you are planning on having multiple servers running on the same network interface at the same time.> Note: In the event of a port conflict, auto-mcs will detect it and temporarily assign another port to your server for the sessionThe default IP address is configured to `localhost:25565`. In this configuration, the server can be accessed over any LAN IP address configured by the machine the software is running on. You can use an IP address on a specific interface if you have multiple NICs/VLANs (e.g. Wi-Fi & Ethernet on two separate networks). These settings are primarily for configuring a LAN server, but there is some more configuration necessary to allow connections via the internet.
# WAN/internet configurationBecause most consumer routers utilize Network Address Translation (NAT), a feature to map multiple LAN devices to a single public IP, port forwarding/triggering or the use of a proxy is required to forward traffic to and from the internet and a LAN device.> Note: Port forwarding comes with a security risk because the port will remain open when the server is not in use. Port triggering or using the built-in proxy is more secure for this reason. If you have administrative access to your router, apply a TCP rule with the LAN port that was configured during setup (default: `25565`) to your router’s port forwarding configuration. If you’ve enabled Bedrock support (Geyser) in the additional settings, you’ll also need to apply a UDP rule for the same port. If your router supports port triggering (more secure), you can enable that for the server’s LAN IP instead. [Learn more about port forwarding here](). If you’re unable to configure your default gateway or your ISP has a strict NAT policy, auto-mcs integrates the playit.gg proxy service which will work any case. After installing your server, you can install and enable playit integration with a single click through the advanced server settings. [Learn more about playit]().# access controlAccess control in auto-mcs encompasses the management of operators, bans, and the whitelist all in one page. For the purposes of initial setup, it’s recommended to grant your own username operator permissions, and configure a whitelist if it’s a private server. For a more detailed overview of access control, [visit the guide](). - additional The additional options screen provides extra configuration depending on the type of server that you’re making. Some of the options listed below may not be available:[Add-on Manager]()Menu to download or import mods & plugins if supported[Access Control]()Modify player permissions like operator status, whitelist, or bansGamemodeDetermines if the world will be survival, creative, or adventureDifficultyModifies how hard the game-play will be. Scales damage, and other game mechanics like hunger. Hardcore is included as a difficulty as wellBedrock support (Geyser)Allows Bedrock clients (mobile, console, etc.) to connect to your server. Checking this box automates the installation of Geyser, Floodgate, and ViaVersion if supported[Learn more about Geyser]()Disable chat reportingFor post-1.19 servers running Spigot, Forge, Paper, or Fabric, this option will install a plugin to prevent Microsoft from reading your chat messages[Learn more about server-side chat signing]()Enable PVPEnable Player-Vs-Player. By default (off), players are unable to damage each otherKeep inventoryPrevents players from losing their inventory on deathEnable spawn protectionPrevents non-operators from modifying blocks in the spawn chunksDaylight & weather cycleDepending on the version, this only changes the daylight cycle. In modern versions, you can easily disable both weather and the daylight cycle for creative mode if desiredSpawn creaturesEnables both hostile and passive mob spawningEnable command blocksAllows command blocks to be used in the worldRandom tick speedModifies the speed of fire spread, crop growth, and other random events. Set to 0 to disable the clock, set higher to increase the chance of random events. Values over 100 can be very resource intensive, use with cautionMax playersChanges the maximum player capacity - Menu to download or import mods & plugins if supported - Modify player permissions like operator status, whitelist, or bans - Determines if the world will be survival, creative, or adventure - Modifies how hard the game-play will be. Vanilla is recommended for most users since it has optimal support for the game mechanics such as Redstone, command blocks, and datapacks. This comes at the cost of performance in some instances. Another advantage of vanilla is that it’s the most up to date as everything else is based on it. When there’s a new update it can take a week or so for other distributions to update as well.

Paper provides numerous advantages over vanilla such as asynchronous chunk loading, rendering enhancements, and Redstone optimization which can be extremely useful with lower-end hardware. Like other CraftBukkit/Spigot-based servers, some of these optimizations can cause issues with stock mechanics like Redstone. In addition to these features, Paper has a suite of cutom plugins and supports all Spigot and CraftBukkit plugins as well. [Learn more about Paper](<https://papermc.io/software/paper>)
content.spigot: Spigot aims to provide an experience as close to vanilla as possible, with the addition of plugin support. It also implements many of the same performance improvements like asynchronous chunk loading. With this in mind, it can be more hardware intensive than Paper depending on the configuration. [Learn more about Spigot](<https://www.spigotmc.org/wiki/about-spigot/>)

(CraftBukkit/Bukkit) has since been forked and superseded by modern solutions such as Paper. It has been provided in auto-mcs for compatibility with legacy servers. [Learn more about CraftBukkit](<https://dev.bukkit.org>)

The Fabric API is automatically included with the installation of Fabric through auto-mcs. Mods need to be installed on both the server and any client that connects. [Learn more about Fabric](<https://fabricmc.net>)
content.forge: Forge is a modding platform with years of support and a large library of additional content. Similar to Fabric, it has server and client-side functionality with the requirement of having mods on both the server and any client that connects. content.server version:
The version of Minecraft you choose is responsible for the core mechanics and features with game-play. It’s recommended to use the latest version (configured by default) for security purposes unless there’s a reason not to:
- Trying unreleased betas (snapshots)
- Utilizing legacy Redstone/command block projects
- Mods that require an older version

Barring this recommendation, auto-mcs supports and can manage every version of Minecraft that’s available. [Learn more about the different versions here](<https://minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Java_Edition_version_history>)Generally, all clients that connect are required to use the same game version that your server is running.

> *Note:*  **If your server runs Paper, Spigot or Fabric, it’s possible to use ViaVersion to enable cross-version capabilities. [Learn more here](<https://github.com/ViaVersion>)**

content.create a new world: (default) this option will generate a server from scratch when the server is started. A custom seed and level type can be specified.

Type in a world name or browse to the root folder of your save. The world will be checked for compatibility and if successful, it will replace the text in the import world input.

After your server is created, the world file can be re-generated or replaced at any time by clicking on ‘Change World File’ in the [server settings](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/settings>).[⠀](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/t/6536de414c5cc352b9ed7506/1698094658062/create-world-input.png) [⠀](https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/t/6536e30ae6deba48204c0485/1698095882528/world-advanced-button.png)

content.import a server:
If you’ve made a server on your own before using auto-mcs, or you want to use a back-up file from another instance of auto-mcs, you can import a server folder or a `.amb`file. The server import feature is on the home screen if there are no servers, or in the Server Manager if there are.

> *Note:*  **auto-mcs does not modify the original server files. Instead, it copies the contents of the server to a local directory and modifies it there. After this, an initial backup is created.**

Any Vanilla, Paper, Spigot, CraftBukkit, Fabric, and Forge server with any version can be imported successfully. If not, auto-mcs may be able to import it but there will likely be issues.
content.post installation:
After creating or importing a server, you’ll be brought to the Server Manager. [Click here to learn more.](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager>)
Although it’s not required, there are some recommended steps to take after installation:
- When the server is stopped, you will be prompted to enable automatic back-ups. Clicking ‘Yes’ will save a snapshot of everything in your server when it’s stopped to be restored later in case of an issue. You can save a back-up in the [Back-up Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/back-ups>) at any time, or by using the `!backup save` command.

> *Note:*  **Regardless of this setting, back-ups will automatically be saved prior to big operations such as an update or changing the world file. There’s also a back-up that’s saved when the server is installed**

- On the topic of back-ups, it’s important to back-up the back-ups in case something happens to your computer. One of the easiest ways to do this is if you have a cloud-hosted storage service. Click on ‘Migrate Back-up Directory’ in the [Back-up Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/back-ups>) and select a sub-folder inside of OneDrive, DropBox Desktop, Google Drive Desktop, etc. You can also click ‘Open Back-up Directory’ and copy the files manually to an external hard drive or something similar.
- If your server isn’t intended to be completely open to the public, take the time to configure proper rules like a whitelist in the [Access Control Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/access-control>) to prevent unwanted guests from joining without permission.
- If you want to change other settings like adding a resource pack, configure the `server.properties` file in the Advanced tab. If you want even more advanced configuration, you can leverage the built in scripting API amscript to accomplish whatever you want. [Learn more about amscript](<https://github.com/macarooni-man/auto-mcs/blob/main/amscript-docs.md>)[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/64dbddec-f8dd-4734-acb8-cbdf845c9617/console-wide.png)

content.overview:
The Server Manager is the gateway of functionality for auto-mcs. After creating or importing your server, the Server Manager is automatically opened. From the home screen, open the overview page to view running servers and mark favorites to keep them at the top.

Upon selecting a server, you’ll be presented with the Launch screen. This panel allows you to launch the server, enter commands, and view performance metrics or interact with players who have joined. Here are a few ways to interact with the panels:
- Click ‘Launch’ or press `ENTER` to start the server
- Left-click on the IP at the top to copy the public IP address, and right-click to copy the LAN address
- Left-click on a user to view more information in the [Access Control Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/access-control>)
- Click the stop button in the top right corner, press `CTRL-Q`, or type `stop` in the console to stop the server
- Click the restart button in the top right corner, press `CTRL-SHIFT-R`, or type `!restart` in the console to restart the server
- Click the top right maximize button or press `F` to full-screen the console panel
- Click on the input at the bottom or press `TAB` to enter commands

Additionally, auto-mcs provides utility commands to operators for administration through the console or in-game chat:
- `!help` to view all available commands
- `!info` to view the console panel properties
- `!restart` to completely stop and start the server in place
- `!backup` to view back-up statistics, save a back-up
- `!acl` to view the banned players, operators, and the whitelist
- `!ams` to enable/disable amscripts, and reload the engine

> *Note:*  **It’s possible to automatically launch your servers with either [task scheduler](<https://www.windowscentral.com/how-create-automated-task-using-task-scheduler-windows-10>) on Windows, or with [cron](<https://cronly.app/news/getting-started-with-cron-jobs-a-beginners-guide>) on Linux. Specify the location of the executable and provide the `--launch` argument to provide a list of server names. Make sure to run these tasks with standard user permissions! `auto-mcs --launch "Server 1, Server 2"`**[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/22c29701-c36e-4a60-81af-22086393aefa/launch-screen.png) [⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/f95b6c2f-cc77-456e-a0f1-f63d69bd9751/server-manager-full.png)

content.overview: Back-ups are often an underlooked but imperative practice. With the former, complexity is the main barrier to creating and maintaining a routine. Because of this, auto-mcs implements a seamless system to create and restore snapshots of your hard work with little intervention.
content.save a back-up:
Creating a back-up is as easy as clicking back-ups on the [taskbar](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager#taskbar>) and then ‘Save Back-up Now’. That’s it!

> *Note:*  **You can also save a back-up in game with the `!backup save` command**

Saving a back-up creates a snapshot in time of the entire server directory:
- All auto-mcs settings
- Server version
- All world files
- Access Control
- All add-ons and state
- server.properties file
- amscript persistent configuration

When saving, auto-mcs will purge the oldest back-up in the configured directory to preserve disk space. To increase or decrease the purge limit, drag the ‘Maximum Back-ups’ slider to the desired value. This behavior can disabled by dragging the ‘Maximum Back-ups’ slider all the way to the right (unlimited).

Additionally, it’s important to back-up the back-ups in case something happens to your computer. One of the easiest ways to do this is if you have a NAS or cloud-hosted storage service. Click on ‘Migrate Back-up Directory’ in the Back-up Manager and select a sub-folder inside of OneDrive, a network share, DropBox Desktop, Google Drive Desktop, etc. You can also click ‘Open Back-up Directory’ and copy the files manually to an external hard drive.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/3fd04ee7-b753-4a17-beea-bdc21935ce96/backup-save.png)
content.restore a back-up:
Restoring a back-up is simple as well. Click on ‘Restore From Back-up’ and select the snapshot in question. The most recent back-up is highlighted, and they are numbered consecutively. This will restore your server in its entirety to the date & time it was saved.

If your server is deleted or you wish to move a server to a different computer, you can import a back-up file through the [Server Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started#import-a-server>).[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/5dcba236-e138-4c42-864d-2b7b01fef672/backup-restore.jpg)
content.automation:
From the Back-up Manager, you can enable automatic back-ups to save a snapshot of your server after it closes. It’s recommended to enable this setting if there’s enough storage space.

> *Note:*  **Regardless of this setting, back-ups will automatically be saved prior to big operations such as an update or changing the world file. There’s also a back-up that’s saved when the server is installed**

This functionality can further be expanded by creating custom behavior with the [amscript API](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/amscript>). For example, here is a script that saves a back-up every hour when a player is present, and when the server is empty:

> *Note:*  **This script can be downloaded and modified by clicking amscript on the [taskbar](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager#taskbar>). Click download and browse for ‘Scheduled Back-ups‘**[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/cb48e904-c942-44d7-87a2-79816af120ed/backup-script.png)

content.overview: Authorization is a fundamental element of computer security, acting as a digital gatekeeper that determines access to your server. Access control is a tool to moderate authorization. In auto-mcs, this concept is implemented as a rudimentary form of [Rule-Based Access Control (RuBAC)](<https://www.networkcomputing.com/network-security/why-your-organization-needs-rule-based-access-control>).
content.rule types:
With this in mind, Minecraft abstracts permissions into bans, whitelists, and operators — all of which moderate authorization with independent rules. Learn more about these types below:
- bans

A ban blocks players from connecting to the server. A ban can be added for a player’s username or IP address. Additionally, with auto-mcs, you can implement IPv4 subnet bans with [CIDR notation](<https://aws.amazon.com/what-is/cidr/>), or a range such as `192.168.1.0-25`. These subnet bans are useful to prevent players from joining if they get a new DHCP address from their ISP for example.

Keep in mind that bans supersede every other rule — meaning no matter the permissions of the affected player, they can’t join if they’re banned.

> *Note:*  **Users can bypass username bans by using another account, and can bypass IP bans by using a VPN/proxy service. To combat this, if you’re using Paper/Spigot certain plugins can block users from connecting with a VPN/proxy [such as this](<https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/%E2%AD%90%EF%B8%8F-vpn-blocker-%E2%AD%90%EF%B8%8F-%E2%9C%85-proxy-detection-%E2%9C%85-anti-bot-%E2%9C%85-anti-proxy-%E2%9C%85-free-fast-async-%E2%9C%85-prevent-hackers.97689/>).**

- whitelist

The whitelist (disabled by default) is an exclusive access list where only specified players can connect. It’s recommended to configure a whitelist for a public-facing server in which there are few people connecting to.

> *Note:*  **Be sure that you have enabled the whitelist in the top left corner. Otherwise, anyone will still be able to connect**

- operators

Operators/Ops are server administrators that can change server settings with in-game commands. Players with this permission are automatically whitelisted as well. Be extremely cautious to whom you grant operator permissions.

Additionally, operators can manage auto-mcs via the built-in [amscript commands](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/amscript>).

content.management:
With the terminology and mechanics explained it’s easier to learn how the Access Control Manager interacts with your server. There is a page dedicated to bans, operators, and the whitelist. On these pages, you can see every player who has connected to the server.

The players listed are referred to as rules which can be modified in a few different ways:
- Right-click a rule to view, and see more options
- Left-click a rule to toggle permission
- Press middle-mouse to toggle the rule globally

Rules can be filtered with the search bar, and can be added with the ‘Add Rules’ button or by pressing `TAB`. The visible list can be switched between pages from the drop-down above the search bar.

Additionally, auto-mcs provides a convenient feature — global rules. With global rules, it’s possible to apply any rule to every server with a single click. These rules will persist when you create or import a server as well. It’s recommended to add your own username as a global operator for ease of management. Visually, a global rule appears with a yellow globe icon on the left.

Visualizing permissions across the rule types can be confusing to determine whether a player has access or not. By right-clicking on any rule, the user panel on the right makes it easy to execute sound decisions by clearly displaying if a player has access, and why. You can also see detailed information such as the UUID or IP geolocation.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/5b65ae4a-a490-434e-a537-043aea39e507/access-control.png) [⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/caca62d2-18ed-4c58-883f-eb1f6a6389da/access-panel.png)

The access control functionality of auto-mcs can further be expanded by creating custom behavior with the [amscript API](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/amscript>). For example, here is a script that takes corrective action on players who use excessive profanity:

> *Note:*  **This script can be downloaded and modified by clicking amscript on the [taskbar](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager#taskbar>). Click download and browse for ‘Profanity Filter‘**[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/f351f515-b85e-4cab-ad9c-60eadafe8fb2/acl-script.png)

content.overview:
Add-ons are an easy way to extend the functionality of your server. From world editing, chat modifications, or hundreds of new weapons & tools, there are a plethora of additions available. Immerse yourself in a realm of endless customization as you shape your Minecraft experience to suit your desires.

In auto-mcs, mods and plug-ins are both referred to as add-ons because they are managed in the same way, but correspond to different distributions:
- Plug-ins are server-side modifications to the game, usually through the [Bukkit API](<https://bukkit.org/pages/about-us/>). This means that assets are reused, and the client doesn’t require any modifications as well.
- Mods are both server-side & client-side meaning that both the client and the server require the mods in use. If the client is missing a mod, or there’s a version mismatch, they can’t connect.

> *Note:*  **Add-ons are only available with a non-vanilla distribution. [Click here to learn more about server distributions](<https://www.auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started?expand=server%20type#advanced-setup>)**
content.installation:
In the [Server Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager>), click ‘Add-ons’ on the [taskbar](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager#taskbar>). There are a few ways to install add-ons to your server.

> *Note:*  **auto-mcs can check for and update most add-ons automatically. Be sure to occasionally check the add-ons tab on the taskbar for updates**
content.download add-ons: The easiest way to install and manage add-ons is to download them directly from auto-mcs. Click download, and then search for an add-on you wish to use. Click on a result and then ‘Install’. You’ll see that it’s now visible in the Add-on Manager. The benefit of this approach is that any add-on downloaded can also be updated automatically.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/0f65ecf6-c7b2-4ac6-8c84-748809de7140/addons.png)
content.import add-ons: If you don’t have access to an internet connection or the add-on you wish to install isn’t available in the repository, you can import `.jar` files by either drag ‘n’ dropping them or selecting them all with the ‘Import’ button. Keep in mind that auto-mcs may or may not be able to update imported add-ons automatically.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/f2c6019b-e495-4931-939d-139338b4f4d8/addon-manager.png)
content.management:
Add-ons have convenient integration with auto-mcs. From the Add-on Manager, you can click to enable/disable add-ons if you don’t wish to uninstall them permanently. This can be useful for testing issues with crashing for example.

> *Note:*  **It’s still possible to delete add-ons by clicking on the trash can icon on the right**

Another useful feature of the Add-on Manager is the update functionality. It will automatically check for updates to provide the latest supported versions of all your add-ons that can be located online. On top of this feature, upon updating or downgrading your server, auto-mcs will upgrade or downgrade all your add-ons to versions that support the change. On this note, all your add-ons will be [backed up prior to a major change](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/back-ups#automation>) such as this.
content.modpacks:
Modpacks are groups of mods curated to work well with each other for a unique and tailored Minecraft experience. Generally, they provide an all-in-one package that contains the `server.jar` along with all the mods and intended configuration for a multiplayer environment. Since these are custom and often packaged inconsistently, it’s difficult to ensure complete compatibility.

To import a modpack, first click [import a new server](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started#import-a-server>) and then import a modpack. Then you can either download one inside the app, or import a `.zip` or `.mrpack` file. Then you can run the server like normal. Due to the volume of mods, if you encounter crashes, try increasing the RAM limit in the settings as well or inspect the server files for a README/version file with directions from the author.

content.overview: The auto-mcs scripting API (amscript) is available to quickly create universal plugins for your auto-mcs servers. It functions primarily as an asynchronous wrapper which fires events from what happens in-game and uses standard Python 3.12 syntax. Because of this mechanic, a single script will work with every Vanilla, CraftBukkit (and derivatives), Forge, and Fabric server regardless of the game version.
content.getting started:
> *Note:*  **If you don’t wish to write scripts yourself or would like to view examples, there’s a built-in repository available from the amscript manager by clicking ‘Download’**

The amscript engine and all of its dependencies are pre-installed and entirely integrated into auto-mcs. You don’t need to download anything to get started! As mentioned previously, amscript is generally based on Python 3.12. If you’re unfamiliar with Python, there are a plethora of resources to learn from [such as this](<https://www.codecademy.com/learn/learn-python-3>). Because of this functionality, you can utilize effectively anything you can do in Python like web requests, OS operations, other APIs, and so much more.

On top of Python, amscript includes an API by default to manage auto-mcs and your server. Additionally, amscript implements events to run code based on in-game activities.

Another useful feature is a fast and simple built-in IDE with API auto-completion, real-time syntax error detection, and familiar keyboard shortcuts. From the [Server Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager>), you can start coding in two clicks without needing to download anything else! You can also download, import, or drag ‘n’ drop scripts. They are shared between every server, but can be enabled/disabled independently.

> *Note:*  **Scripts are not backed up automatically by the [Back-up Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/back-ups>). Click on the folder icon in the top right and copy them elsewhere, or even write a script to back them up!**[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/0df44a79-c4b2-436f-8ab4-6c324893a90e/amscript-manager.png)
content.api & events:
The amscript API provides modules to interact with auto-mcs (imported by default). Additionally, there are events driven by special decorators. These events are triggered by certain conditions in-game to run snippets of code.

For a comprehensive reference of the module & event syntax, arguments, and methods, consider viewing the [API documentation](<https://github.com/macarooni-man/auto-mcs/blob/main/amscript-docs.md>).
content.amscript ide:
You don’t need any special software or tools to take advantage of the power of amscript. This development environment is included directly with the installation of auto-mcs.
## controls

Inside the [Server Manager](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager>), create a new script or edit an existing one to open the amscript IDE. Here’s a reference to common controls in the editor:
- Right-click the background to view the context menu of options
- Press `CTRL-C` to copy and `CTRL-V` to paste
- Press `CTRL-Z` to undo and `CTRL-R` to redo
- Press `CTRL-F` to find and `CTRL-H` to find & replace
- Press `TAB` to indent and `SHIFT-TAB` to unindent
- Press `CTRL-/` to toggle comments
- Press `CTRL-PLUS` or `CTRL-MINUS` to change font size
- `amscript`  Toggle, download, or import scripts[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/3a711338-428a-4381-93a1-4b13ef03e98f/amscript-ide.png)
content.saving & modification:
As you’re editing your script, the IDE will auto-save. There’s no need to worry about losing your progress.

> *Note:*  **If editing a script while the server is running, you’ll need to reload the amscript engine by clicking ‘Reload Scripts’ in the top right corner of the Script Manager. You can also use the `!ams reload` command in the console or in-game chat**
content.auto-completion: With the addition of custom modules and events, auto-completion makes it easier to reference available methods and syntax. Press `TAB`/`ENTER` to fill in the entirety of a method or event call. You can also press the `🡡`/`🡣` keys to switch between different auto-complete suggestions.
content.error detection:
Simple syntactic errors in the IDE are displayed inline with a red highlight, and the error itself is shown in the bottom right corner. Clicking on the error text will scroll to the line.

Deferred code (in function execution) is not able to be processed until runtime. You may see errors for more complex issues in the server console.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/d199b455-6256-4c52-a3cf-bc7d095001c2/error-example.png)
content.external modules:
To further elaborate on Python integration, it’s entirely possible to create your own modules or install them from [PyPI](<https://pypi.org>) with pip.

First, verify that the amscript `libs` folder is available. In the top right corner of the amscript manager, click on the folder icon to open the amscript directory and look for the folder there. If it doesn’t exist, create it. Make sure that you have a valid [Python 3.12 ](<https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-31212/>)[installation](<https://www.python.org/downloads/release/python-3918/>) to utilize the pip package manager.

> *Note:*  **Keep in mind that amscript files have a file extension of `.ams`, and all libraries have a `.py` extension. Libraries are unable to use the amscript modules or events**
content.windows installation:
Open a Command Prompt and run the following command:
`pip install --target "%appdata%\.auto-mcs\Tools\amscript\libs" <package-name>`
content.linux installation:
Open a terminal and run the following command:
`pip install --target ~/.auto-mcs/Tools/amscript/libs <package-name>`
content.macos installation:
Open a terminal and run the following command:
`pip install --target "~/Library/Application Support/auto-mcs/Tools/amscript/libs" <package-name>`
content.custom modules: Writing a module works the same way it would in a normal Python environment. In such cases, it’s beneficial to utilize a more in-depth IDE such as [PyCharm](<https://www.jetbrains.com/pycharm/>) or [Spyder](<https://www.spyder-ide.org>). This guide won’t go over writing modules, though you can [learn more here](<https://www.digitalocean.com/community/tutorials/how-to-write-modules-in-python-3>). Make sure to place them in the `libs` folder detailed above.

content.overview: Along with the distinct management of back-ups, access control, add-ons, and scripting, there are a variety of other configurations available. From updates to world management, the settings page allows you to modify most aspects of your server.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/3f685ca6-0a2b-41a7-aebe-2a9a59e93890/advanced.png)
content.general:
This editor provides a tailored experience to the `server.properties` file provided for haste edits to the advanced server configuration. By default, auto-mcs provides an optimized configuration. If you would like to customize it yourself with a custom resource pack for example, there’s a [reference of all the available features](<https://minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Server.properties>).

In the editor provided, you can search for keys, press `SPACE` to toggle boolean values, and undo/redo as expected. The editor is safe and won’t let you break the configuration on accident. With this in mind, it’s not possible to add new keys for this very reason. If the configuration file needs to be replaced, click on the next button ‘Open Server Directory’ to edit the file directly.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/5f513e23-e420-4d57-8b60-315ebffea700/properties-editor.png)
content.open server directory:
Although generally unnecessary in most situations, this shortcut is provided to access the server files directly. Certain add-ons require advanced configuration that is currently unsupported by auto-mcs.

> *Note:*  **Take caution when editing or adding new files and use the [back-up feature](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/back-ups#save-a-backup>) prior to modification.**
content.memory usage:
Seemingly straight-forward, memory usage is the maximum allotment of [memory dedicated to the Java Virtual Machine](<https://docs.oracle.com/cd/E13150_01/jrockit_jvm/jrockit/geninfo/diagnos/garbage_collect.html>) (JVM) for your server when it’s started.

By default, when the slider is set to auto, auto-mcs will automatically adjust memory allocation based on system availability and the configuration of your server. On the topic of memory, auto-mcs also makes adjustments to the garbage collector to optimize the heap space and collection interval.

> *Note:*  **It’s recommended to increase this setting only upon recieving crashes due to `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space`**
content.network: This combo box allows you to modify both the IP address and port simultaneously. To learn more, [refer to the Getting Started guide](<https://www.auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started?expand=networking#advanced-setup>).
content.enable proxy/install playit:
If you’re unable to configure your default gateway or your ISP has a strict NAT policy, auto-mcs integrates the playit.gg proxy service which works in every case.

To enable the playit service, you’ll need to install it by clicking the “Install Playit” button in the server settings. Once installed, you’ll see a toggle switch in place of the install button to enable the agent. That’s it, auto-mcs will configure playit tunnels automatically! You can run up to 4 tunnels concurrently. [Learn more about playit](<https://playit.gg>).
content: This button will permanently delete your server. There is no undoing this action. Before your server is deleted, there will be a complete back-up created that can be imported later, or to another instance of auto-mcs. [See the Getting Started guide to learn more](<https://auto-mcs.com/guides/getting-started#import-a-server>).
content.updates: Enabling this switch will automatically update your server to the latest version when available. When updating, auto-mcs will automatically create a back-up before any changes to your server. This will also attempt to update all of your add-ons.
content.update now: If available, this button manually updates to the latest version that’s available. When updating, auto-mcs will automatically create a back-up before any changes to your server. This will also attempt to update all of your add-ons.
content.transilience: Edit the name in this box and press `ENTER` to rename your server to something else.
content.change world file: With this button, you can either create a new world or select a world file to replace the one in your server with. This action will automatically create a back-up before any changes are made.

content.overview: If you’re away from home or wish to access a server on another computer, remote management is an enticing concept. Due to this potential, auto-mcs includes the simplest custom remote framework available. Telepath is exceptionally transparent, secure, and responsive while retaining the same intuitive interface from local operations.
content.how it works:
Telepath allows you to seamlessly pair instances of auto-mcs together. The standard application can both access other instances of auto-mcs, or be accessed from another instance of auto-mcs. Each device intended as a client will need to download the application and follow the pairing process detailed below.

In presentation, remote servers will appear as a normal server in the [Server Manager](<https://www.auto-mcs.com/guides/server-manager>) prepended with the server’s nickname and denoted with the wireless icon. Additionally, everything that can be done on a local server is available remotely; whether you’re drag-n-dropping add-ons to upload, importing a server, or even using the [amscript IDE](<https://www.auto-mcs.com/guides/amscript#amscript-ide>). Like the other features of auto-mcs, you don’t need any external software or utilities to leverage the framework.

In more technical terms, Telepath is a [REST-ful API](<https://www.redhat.com/en/topics/api/what-is-a-rest-api>) used to communicate with other instances of auto-mcs via web endpoints. By default, Telepath communicates HTTP traffic over TCP port `7001`. Most of the functionality is abstracted and happens behind the scenes. Logins are automatic, and interaction is initiated by pairing, described in detail below. Although it’s a web protocol, it cannot be accessed via a browser, and is intended to be managed by another instance of the app through the GUI.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/725e53ff-d401-426d-a663-bd340e8535c3/overview.png)
content.headless setup:
While headless operation is not required to use Telepath, auto-mcs supports a minimal terminal interface on both Linux and macOS for running a Telepath host on a headless server like a VPS. This mode supports basic functionality such as creating servers from a template, editing the `server.properties`, a full console representative of the GUI, and Telepath management. The intention of headless mode is for conserving resources on a system that’s infrequently accessed, and therefore is intended that any advanced management is to be done with a paired Telepath client through the GUI.

On supported operating systems, headless mode can be launched with `./auto-mcs --headless`. If your server doesn’t have a desktop environment, headless mode will be launched by default in the current TTY. It’s recommended to [use a multiplexer](<https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki>) to maintain TTY access if needed. A full command reference can be obtained by pressing `?` or by entering `help` in the headless CLI (command-line interface).

Additionally, a [Docker image](<https://hub.docker.com/r/macarooniman/auto-mcs>) is available that wraps the headless functionality of auto-mcs to access the CLI through a web browser. Since the Docker image is essentially a web wrapper for the CLI, any reference to headless also applies to the Docker image unless otherwise specified.
content.pairing:
Pairing through Telepath is quite a simple process. Here, we’ll refer to the “server” as the remote device you’re accessing, and the “client” as your local instance that’s reaching out to the “server.”

> *Note:*  **Telepath is a protocol that operates over TCP. This means that if the server isn't on the same network you'll need to port forward, just like a Minecraft server. You can also use domain names in place of an IPv4 address.**

To access the Telepath menu, expand the “settings” button on the main menu (in the bottom right corner), or from the search anywhere else[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/d5046ff1-01ad-4f1f-a178-9094fb995fd4/telepath-button.png)
content.pairing from the gui:
After the instances are paired, the button “manage instances” will appear in the client, and “manage users” will appear on the server. From here, you can rename or un-pair Telepath instances. On the server, you can also temporarily prevent specific users from connecting with the hot switch.

From headless mode, the management command reference can be viewed with `telepath ?` from the CLI.[⠀](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/6525da8272c3ad522c663487/a3ce34ab-5fbb-401d-8803-b5f40c0d3314/user-manager.png)
content.security:
By default, Telepath initializes connections over HTTP – meaning that the traffic can be seen in plain text. For authentication, Telepath integrates a custom [Public Key Infrastructure (PKI)](<https://www.okta.com/identity-101/public-key-infrastructure/>) within HTTP to encrypt authentication traffic. The entirety of the login and logout process is automatic, and invisible to the user.

> *Note:*  **Keep in mind that any action other than authentication will remain in plain text.**

Additionally, sessions are secured by network origin and unique tokens; one used for pairing, and another for the session. Attempts to subvert a live or expired session will be logged and blocked by default. This log can be accessed in (relative to the auto-mcs directory) `./Tools/telepath/audit-logs`

Due to the nature of generic session traffic being unencrypted, it’s recommended to tunnel Telepath through a VPN. We recommend using a standalone instance of [OpenVPN](<https://openvpn.net/>) on the network of the host, and port forwarding that traffic instead of Telepath itself. If it’s not possible to dedicate a server to a VPN, a simpler solution would be to set up a service such as [WireGuard](<https://www.wireguard.com/>) on the host machine itself.

For security disclosures or feedback, please [get in touch with us directly via email](<mailto:help@auto-mcs.com?subject=Security%20Disclosure%20-%20>).
